title: Pilot acceptance rubric & SLA triggers - sign-off
summary: Final sign-off on pilot acceptance rubric, agreed go/no-go thresholds for latency, throughput and quality, confirmed reporting format (CSV + weekly dashboard), and outlined test harness and timeline for benchmark runs. Security checklist items noted for Private deployment evaluation.
next_steps: Redwood to deliver test harness and sample runbook by 2025-12-02
VelaData to provide 3 production prompts + labeled ground truth by 2025-12-05
Schedule first benchmark run week of 2025-12-08
Security follow-up with SSO/KMS details by 2025-12-03
action_items: Jordan Blake - Share test harness repo + cost model spreadsheet - due 2025-12-02
Priya Nambiar - Create benchmark run template (CSV columns + scripts) - due 2025-12-02
Alex Mercer - Provide 3 canonical prompt sets and expected outputs - due 2025-12-05
Samira Khan - Confirm target RPS and peak windows with infra team - due 2025-12-01
David Ortiz - Send SOC2 report excerpt and list of additional security questions - due 2025-12-03
transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2025-11-28 16:00 UTC | Duration: 60 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Blake, Priya Nambiar (Redwood); Alex Mercer, Samira Khan, David Ortiz (VelaData)
[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone thanks for hopping on — quick roll call?
[00:06] Alex: Alex here, hi.
[00:08] Samira: Samira.
[00:10] David: David here.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Priya from our SE team is on to run through the acceptance rubric and the benchmark plan. Priya, you want to kick off?
[00:20] Priya: Yep, thanks Jordan. Hi Alex, Samira, David. First off the goal for today is a sign-off on the acceptance rubric — we want to align on concrete go/no-go thresholds for latency, throughput, and model quality plus the reporting format so both sides know what success looks like.
[00:36] Alex: Sounds good. Quick context, our primary workload is a customer support summarization + reranking flow. We expect a 1.5k average input tokens, peak concurrency 120 RPS for inference across our multi-tenant service during morning batch windows.
[00:51] Priya: Got it. Can you confirm whether those 1.5k are trimmed or full transcripts?
[00:55] Alex: Full transcripts — so there's some variance, maybe 800 to 3k tokens.
[01:00] Priya: OK that influences our batching and KV cache sizing.
[01:05] Jordan: Quick note on pilot mode: we recommend two parallel benchmark tracks — a latency-focused small-batch run to verify 95th percentile SLOs and a throughput-focused long-run to validate sustained tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens.
[01:21] Samira: For us the high-level business gate is user-visible latency. If 95th is above 300 ms for summarization, leadership won't sign off.
[01:29] David: From security side we also need to confirm data handling for the pilot — whether logs are persisted, KMS usage, and SSO integration for the private deploy.
[01:38] Priya: Understood. On the acceptance thresholds we've proposed the following — feel free to push back: 95th percentile latency for end-to-end summarization: <= 250 ms for hosted variants, <= 150 ms for dedicated configuration in the pilot; throughput target: sustain 4k tokens/sec per instance-class (we'll map to your GPU type in the harness); quality target: Rouge-L >= 0.78 or within 5% of your current baseline on labeled set; cost target: under $X per 1M tokens (we'll fill exact number after cost modeling).
[02:09] Alex: Two quick questions — first, 150 ms 95th seems tight for long prompts (2k+). Second, quality metric — our current baseline Rouge-L is 0.82, so 5% delta would be 0.78, ok.
[02:21] Priya: For long prompts we plan to enable prefix caching and continuous batching; the 150 ms is for dedicated tuned cluster with quantization. We'll call out fallback to larger model variant if quality dips.
[02:33] Jordan: Also note that for go/no-go we want to avoid single-number pass/fail. We'll use a scoring rubric across latency, quality, and cost, with weighted thresholds. The rule of thumb we discussed: latency 40% weight, quality 40% weight, cost 20% weight. If aggregate score >= 85% it's a go; between 70-85% it's conditional with mitigations; <70% is no-go.
[02:53] Samira: That weighted approach seems reasonable. Can you show how the scoring maps to real numbers?
[02:58] Priya: Sure — example mapping: for latency, 95th <=150 ms = 100 pts, 150-250 ms = linear down to 60 pts, >250 ms = 0; for quality, within baseline =100, within 5% = 80, >10% drop = 0; cost: below target =100, up to 1.5x target = 50, >1.5x = 0. We'll produce the rubric spreadsheet.
[03:23] Alex: Ok that helps. One more thing — we need per-route SLOs. The summarization route stricter than rerank route.
[03:30] Priya: We'll include per-route thresholds in the CSV template.
[03:34] Jordan: On reporting format, VelaData said they'd prefer a single CSV with a results row per run + a weekly dashboard snapshot. Priya — what's in the CSV?
[03:43] Priya: Columns: run_id, timestamp, model_variant, config_notes, avg_input_tokens, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, total_tokens, cost_estimate_usd, rouge_l, exact_match_pct, sample_failures_link. We'll attach a sample run.
[03:59] Samira: We'll need the sample failures link to point to a controlled S3 bucket in our VPC so security can inspect without data leak.
[04:07] David: Correct — S3 with VPC endpoint and KMS key we control. Also need audit logs of inference payloads and access to the run artifacts for at least 90 days.
[04:17] Priya: For the hosted pilot we can stream logs to your S3 using customer-managed KMS; for Private we'll run entirely inside a VPC with your KMS and audit log forwarding. We'll document both modes.
[04:30] Alex: About the test harness — what will we run on our side vs Redwood?
[04:34] Priya: We'll deliver the harness (Python scripts + Docker) that can run against hosted endpoints or your private cluster. Minimal steps: seed corpus upload, run runner to spin up concurrent clients with tokenization aligned, collect metrics into CSV. We will run first benchmark on Redwood side with mirrored dataset (sanitized) to ensure parity, then hand over to VelaData for on-prem run.
[04:57] Jordan: Timeline check: we propose Redwood delivers harness + rubric by 2025-12-02. VelaData provides prompts and labeled outputs by 2025-12-05. First validation run by Redwood week of 2025-12-08 followed by on-prem run week of 2025-12-15. Does that align?
[05:13] Alex: That timeline looks ok, we need to confirm internal sign-offs but it's plausible.
[05:17] Samira: We will need a day for infra to provision VPC endpoints, probably target 2025-12-10 for infra readiness.
[05:24] David: Security sign-off needs SOC2 artifacts and a short answers doc about data retention and encryption — I'll share questions by Wednesday.
[05:32] Priya: Noted. Regarding acceptance reporting cadence — we'll produce a final benchmark report (PDF) plus raw CSV and the scoring spreadsheet. The scoring spreadsheet will show per-run scoring and aggregated weighted score.
[05:45] Alex: If the pilot goes no-go because of latency but quality is clearly better, what's our mitigation? Can Redwood propose a canary route mixing dedicated and hosted?
[05:55] Jordan: Yes — one of the approved mitigations is mixed routing — route 80% to dedicated for latency-sensitive traffic and 20% to hosted higher-capacity models for quality-sensitive requests. We'll document rollback and fallback policies.
[06:08] Samira: Will the billing for the pilot be separate? We need cost transparency.
[06:12] Jordan: We'll provide cost breakdown per run (tokens, GPU-hours, infra). For Dedicated pilot we can provide estimated monthly cost and an optional reserved capacity quote.
[06:21] Alex: On metrics, please include memory footprint and KV cache hit rates in the output for us to tune sequence length handling.
[06:28] Priya: Yes — we'll include KV cache hit %, GPU memory usage, and tail-latency distribution columns.
[06:34] David: Also include a short security appendix in the report listing SSO, KMS, retention, and data deletion process.
[06:40] Priya: We'll append a Security Appendix template.
[06:43] Jordan: Anything else on go/no-go thresholds?
[06:46] Alex: One last item — tolerance for intermittent errors. We can tolerate up to 0.2% 5xx for the pilot, anything above requires investigation.
[06:55] Priya: We'll capture error rate as a metric and include automatic alerts in the runbook.
[06:59] Jordan: OK let's recap and confirm next steps.
[07:03] Priya: Recap: Redwood to share test harness repo, scoring spreadsheet, and sample CSV by 2025-12-02. VelaData to provide canonical prompts and labels by 2025-12-05. Redwood will run initial benchmark 2025-12-08 and share results. Security follow-up for KMS/SSO by 2025-12-03.
[07:22] Alex: Sounds good, we'll review and confirm. Thanks everyone.
[07:26] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links. End meeting.
notes: Agreed weighted scoring rubric (latency 40%, quality 40%, cost 20%)
CSV reporting schema agreed and sample columns listed
Security requirements for S3 + KMS + audit logs captured
Timeline with key dates: harness 12-02, prompts 12-05, Redwood run week of 12-08, on-prem run week of 12-15
